title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-6
content:
Background:
- Regression observed 2026-02-10 on prod-dedicated-us-west cluster (pool: rwd-dedicated-gpu-pool-3).
- Symptoms: sustained 25-35% drop in throughput (tokens/sec) for typical chat workloads; p99 latency increased ~2x during peak.
- Suspected area: continuous batching logic + KV-cache interaction after the kernel changes in PR #1287.

What I saw (high-level):
- Before regression baseline (2026-01): 12k tokens/sec aggregate, p50 ~40ms, p99 ~220ms.
- After change (2026-02-10 morning): 8.5k tokens/sec, p50 ~55ms, p99 ~420ms.
- Error/metric spikes correlate with autoscaler events and batch formation timeouts.

Immediate reproduction steps I ran locally:
1) Start local runtime with model-variant: redwood/gptx-4b-qat (config: quant=8, kv_cache=true, cbatch=true).
   - docker-compose run --rm runtime
2) Run synthetic load (replay trace from 2026-02-09 peak):
   - python tools/loadtest.py --trace traces/2026-02-09-peak.json --concurrency 120 --duration 10m --report perf.csv
3) Observe throughput baseline vs after toggling CBATCH flag:
   - With cbatch=true: avg tokens/sec 900 (matches degraded behavior)
   - With cbatch=false: avg tokens/sec 1250 (closer to expected)

Commands / logs captured:
- grep for batch-timeouts:
  $ kubectl logs --since=2h -l app=runtime -n dedicated | grep "batch_timeout" -n | head -20  
  2026-02-10T08:17:02Z runtime-0 "batch_timeout: formed_batch_id=3421 size=1 waited_ms=1500"
  2026-02-10T08:18:03Z runtime-1 "batch_timeout: formed_batch_id=3432 size=1 waited_ms=1600"

- Example runtime warning (truncated):
  [WARN] 2026-02-10T08:17:02Z batching/queue.go:312 batch_timeout formed_batch_id=3421 size=1 waited_ms=1500 
  stack: batching.nextBatch() -> batchForming.wait() -> scheduleKernel()

- KV-cache debug lines:
  [INFO] 2026-02-10T08:17:02Z kv-cache/cache.go:121 miss model=redwood/gptx-4b-qat key=conv-abc-123
  [DEBUG] 2026-02-10T08:17:02Z kv-cache/metrics.go:44 eviction_trigger=true candidate_size=24MB

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Continuous batching is mis-sized so short requests are not coalescing (too-small batch window after kernel change) causing many size=1 batches and kernel launch overhead dominating.
2) KV-cache eviction or locking is blocking batch assembly (cache lookups are synchronous and add ~10-30ms per request).
3) Autoscaler churn (scale-down then scale-up) introduced cold-workers that take longer to warm KV cache and lead to transient timeouts that propagate into batch formation.
4) A regression in kernel selection heuristics (PR #1287) increased kernel startup latency on certain sequence-length distributions.

What I tried so far (notes + results):
- Toggle CBATCH window: increased batch_window from 5ms -> 15ms in runtime config, re-ran load: throughput improves ~12% but p99 still high (suggests partial mitigation).
- Switch KV-cache to async (experimental branch): local test showed 20ms reduction in median for similar trace but increased memory—needs more validation.
- Rollback PR #1287 on staging: staging throughput matched pre-regression baseline (strong signal that PR is implicated).
- Add tracing around batchForming.wait() to measure per-request contributions: found median wait contributed 18ms, but long tail at >1500ms corresponds to batch_timeout logs.

Quick diffs I examined (notes):
- PR #1287 changed: scheduling.go kernelSelection() to prefer "low-latency" kernels for seq_len < 64, but introduced a synchronous kernel warm-up (warmKernelSync()) path.
- warmKernelSync() calls cudaInit() and blocks the worker thread until warm-up done. Previously warm-ups were async via background goroutine.

Correlated data points:
- Most affected requests are short-turn chat messages (seq_len < 64) which align with kernelSelection change.
- Batch size distribution for impacted time window: 63% size=1, 25% size=2, 12% size>=3 (compared to baseline 30% size=1).
- Node-level metrics: high GPU utilization but low concurrency per-worker; CPU spikes when warmKernelSync runs.

Repro script snippets (for my future self):
- run with environment flags: RUNTIME_CBAT_WINDOW_MS=15 RUNTIME_KV_ASYNC=true RUNTIME_KERNEL_WARMUP=async
- loadtest command: python tools/loadtest.py --trace traces/2026-02-09-peak.json --concurrency 120 --duration 10m --out degraded.csv

Next steps (priority order):
1) Roll forward a patch to replace warmKernelSync() with async warm path and add a startup gating metric so first request pays warm cost without blocking batch assembly. (owner: Miguel)
2) Add KV-cache lookup instrumentation (histograms) and convert hot-path lookups to async where safe. (owner: Priya)
3) Experimentally increase cbatch window to 20ms in a canary pool and monitor throughput/latency tradeoffs. (owner: me)
4) Add a temporary heuristic: if formed_batch.size==1 and wait_ms > 200 then extend window for next X requests for that route. (risk: complexity)
5) Postmortem draft: collect timeline, diff, and rollback notes for INF-3421.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the higher memory usage from async KV acceptable for Dedicated customers? Need finance/infra input.
- How to avoid increasing latency for large-batch workloads when increasing cbatch window? Need smarter per-route heuristics.
- Is kernel warmup cost variable across GPU types (A10 vs A100) enough to require per-node warm strategies?

Incident breadcrumbs (timeline):
- 2026-02-09 23:12 UTC: PR #1287 merged to main (non-blocking review notes).
- 2026-02-10 07:45 UTC: first alerts from dedicated-us-west about increased p99 latency.
- 2026-02-10 08:03 UTC: Ops temporarily increased cbatch window to 15ms on pool-3; partial improvement.
- 2026-02-10 11:30 UTC: Rollback of PR #1287 to staging for validation.
- 2026-02-11 09:10 UTC: Initial root-cause suspected (warmKernelSync) after local reproductions.

Notes to include in postmortem draft:
- Timeline + signal graphs (need ops to export).
- Diff that introduced synchronous warmup.
- Small but high-impact change: warmKernelSync intended to reduce cold-start tail but caused head-of-line blocking for batching.
- Proposed mitigation: async warmup + short circuit for batch assembly, and safer kernel selection flag gated behind rollout.

Misc (random thoughts):
- Could we instrument the client SDK to attach a small "is_latency_sensitive" hint so we can steer those into a low-latency kernel path without breaking batching?
- Might be worth re-evaluating the default cbatch window per model-variant; we currently use one global default which isn't optimal across seq distributions.

End of scratchpad.

(Will move actionable items to INF-3421 and create a canary config change PR after confirmation.)
